entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gaius of Ephesus was a prominent Christian bishop and one of the Seventy Disciples, appointed by Jesus Christ.

Gaius of Ephesus is numbered among the Seventy Disciples, and was Bishop of Ephesus in the early Christian era. He played a significant role in the spread of Christianity in Asia Minor, particularly in the city of Ephesus. The Eastern Orthodox Church and Roman Catholic Church remember St. Gaius on January 4 among the Seventy, and on November 5.

As a leader in the early Christian community, Gaius of Ephesus was instrumental in shaping the theology and practices of the Church. He was a key figure in the development of the Didache, a Christian text that outlines the principles of Christian living. His teachings and writings had a lasting impact on the early Christian church, shaping its understanding of baptism, Eucharist, and other key practices.
